I deleted the extension I created (deployment, service and both ConfigMaps).

Drove all five against the installed bundle, and the regression the last round found is gone. CLI: 'Show raw output' on screen 03 expands in one click and renders the pod's real log (vue-cli-service serve output with timestamps, 'DONE Compiled successfully in 2703ms'); the HTTP 406 is fixed, devServerLog now sends no Accept header and says why in a comment. The Terminal tab attaches a live xterm (canvas present) to the pod's tmux session, and I read my own prompts back out of it with `tmux capture-pane -t mc-editor` three separate times. FILES: /barn/extensions/base/files lists the tree, marks NEW/EDITED and opens a file in the editor pane. GITHUB IMPORT: the Import dialog does connection as step one inside itself ('There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own to send you to'), with no link out to settings. PUBLISH: the dialog reads the version and the changed files out of the pod and lists each destination separately. SETTINGS: /barn/settings renders sign-off policy, GitHub connection, assistant permissions, preview target, access and what is sent to the model. Nothing regressed through the changed exec layer either: every write I made this run went through it and landed in the pod (a comment, a send-to-assistant, a per-file revert, a discard, a commit from Approve, a brief edit that rewrote BRIEF.md).

Two routes, both land in the same place. From a hunk: 'Send to the assistant' put my exact sentence into the pod's session ('Their words: w5-review-cross probe: send this one to the assistant please.. Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did.'). From the decision bar: 'Request changes' recorded the rejection and then routed me to /dashboard/barn/editor/base?tab=terminal, with the pane holding 'A reviewer looked at the working tree of the base extension and asked for a change: <my paragraph>. Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did.' The reviewer writes a sentence, not a fix, and the author still has to act on it.

Built the case on demo: set refs/barn/published/local to the then-HEAD, committed verify-w5-committed.md, and left verify-w5-working.md uncommitted. The review screen showed one diff of two files measured from that baseline, with no per-commit history and no intermediate state, and named the point out loud ('this list is measured against the last version published into this Rancher'). Screen 12 says the same thing when narrowing: 'The whole change, measured from the last published version, is 2 files.' I reset demo afterwards.

Drove the permission mode in both directions. Screen 03's strip chip is a real control: its menu offers 'Edits apply without asking', 'File edits apply, everything else asks', 'Planning only, no edits' and 'claude decides what to ask about', and picking the second one changed the chip. Screen 09 did not follow: its radio group still had 'Do not ask at all' checked afterwards, and the group is explicitly marked not settable ([data-testid=settings-permission-fixed], 'Not settable, and not per user. The pod starts claude...'). Clicking a different radio there changes nothing.
verdicts.defect: Two defects against this rule. (1) The permission mode is not one state in two places: screen 03 sets the live session's mode and screen 09 reports the pod's start-up mode, and after changing it on 03 the two disagreed with no indication that they are different things. (2) A second surface still edits the GitHub token: the editor settings modal opened from [data-testid=barn-editor-settings-button] on screen 03 contains a password field [data-testid=barn-settings-token] placeholder 'ghp_...' that writes the token, alongside screen 09's own connection card. That modal is the 'bare GitHub token modal' the redesign says it replaces.

verdicts.evidence: Wrote a distinctive criterion on screen 10 ('w5rc marker criterion: the queue lists only handed-over work') into the fourth Acceptance criterion field; the page saved it ('Saved 11:07 PM') and BRIEF.md in the pod gained '- [ ] w5rc marker criterion...' under '## How we will know it worked'. Screen 12 then listed it verbatim among its four criteria with the state 'not measured', and screen 13 listed it as item 4 of the walked checklist with Yes / No / Can't tell / Show me against it. Nothing was re-entered anywhere. I restored BRIEF.md byte for byte afterwards (md5 matches the backup).

Inspected the rendered markup. The Studio is built from its own S-prefixed primitives in pkg/barn/components/ui (SButton, SChip, SBanner, SCard, STabs, SMenu, SModal), not from the dashboard's. Screen 01's table is a div grid with class 'studio-home__table' and hand-rolled 'studio-home__th' headers: document.querySelector('.sortable-table') is null and no element under it carries a sortable-table class.
verdicts.defect: Screen 01 is a bespoke table, not the SortableTable pattern the rationale row names ('the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page'), so the claim that a Rancher user already knows how to read it does not hold. The wider claim is met in spirit (nothing needs a new primitive) but not in fact (the primitives are new implementations of existing ones).

verdicts.evidence: Seeded a recorded failure and opened screen 08. It named the cause in words, offered 'Ask the assistant to explain this', 'Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Show me pages/NodeHealth.vue' and, for the way back, 'Roll back to the snapshot "autosave 2314 on Aug 23"' taken 25 seconds earlier, with 'Undo the last change' beside it. The snapshots are real: refs/tags/barn-snap/* in the pod holds dozens of automatic ones, so a failure always has a point to return to. The screen is also honest about the limit of the guarantee rather than overselling it: 'no build of this extension has succeeded here yet, so this is the nearest point that exists rather than a build that is known to have worked', and 'Rolling back snapshots the failed tree first, so nothing you have done is lost'. I did not press it, since a rollback would take other verifiers' work with it.

Everything I did before the publish dialog asked nobody. Created an extension, wrote and reverted files, discarded a whole working tree, switched diff modes, commented, sent a comment to the assistant, opened the live preview, edited the brief and opened the failure screen with its rollback offer, on three different extensions. No approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no disabled control appeared at any point. The only 'Requires approval' and 'The gate' chips in the product are on the two distribution rows of the publish dialog, and the local install row is chipped 'No sign-off'.

The publish dialog names exactly one hard gate and puts it at the distribution boundary: 'Push to an OCI repository. The gate. The one hard gate in the design: the point an extension becomes installable by people who did not build it, and the only step that asks anybody for permission.' 'Load into this Rancher' beside it is chipped 'No sign-off' and reversible ('"Remove local install" takes it back off'). Nothing earlier in the walk (01, 02, 10, 03, 04) asked for an approval. The OCI push itself is not built and the dialog says so plainly rather than drawing a button that lies: 'The gate in front of it works; the push itself does not exist, and a button that pretended otherwise would be worse than this sentence.'

The reading half is now right and it is this round's fix: the chip and the queue read the PR out of the packet record rather than from the branch, so they work with no token and would survive the PR being merged (packet.pr is rendered by queue-pr-<name> and by rc-pr, and where there is no packet the chip says 'Not handed over yet'). What I could not do is produce the record, because crossing the gate produces nothing here.
verdicts.defect: Neither route across the gate can create the PR in this product as installed. 'Push to an OCI repository' is 'Not built' by the dialog's own admission, and 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' / 'Push the source to GitHub' needs a GitHub token that Studio has no way to obtain by itself ('There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own'). So the hand-off record the flow map calls 'the PR is the record' cannot be produced by the one hard gate at all, and the seeded packet on base carries pr: null.

verdicts.evidence: base has had a dirty working tree throughout this run and nothing about it reached anybody: `kubectl get uiplugins -A` lists only barn and nodehealth, and base's own row on screen 01 offers 'Remove the local install' greyed out with the reason 'not installed'. The review screen says the same in words ('These changes are running in your preview only', 'Nothing here has reached the repository yet'), and publishing is a separate deliberate act behind a confirmation modal that spells out the consequence ('Everybody signed into this cluster gets the new build the next time they load a page'). Snapshots are taken per build (refs/tags/barn-snap/*, the newest 25 seconds old when I looked).

The path exists end to end in the product (provenanceFor() blames each line back to the turn that committed it, the strip renders per hunk, the brief travels with the change and is shown in the packet column, and I proved the brief half by writing a criterion on screen 10 and reading it back on 12 and 13). The prompt half cannot be exercised: claude in every pod in this cluster answers 'Not logged in . Please run /login', so no turn can run, nothing can commit a turn id, and both pods report no provenance ('this pod was started before the Studio recorded provenance' on nodehealth, 'no prompt recorded' on base). Authoring a change with two distinguishable prompts is not possible until the pod's assistant is signed in.

Opened the row menu for each extension on /barn/extensions. nodehealth, which is installed as a UIPlugin (cattle-ui-plugin-system/nodehealth v0.1.0), offers an enabled 'Remove the local install v0.1.0'. base and demo, which are not installed, show the same item disabled with the reason on it ('not installed'). So the list is where a live extension is taken back, and the item states its own applicability rather than being hidden.

Both amber routes end in the same workspace. Rejection: 'Request changes' on screen 12 routed me to /dashboard/barn/editor/base?tab=terminal with the comment already in the assistant's session, not to a remediation screen. Build failure: screen 08's actions are all workspace actions ('Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Undo the last change', 'Roll back to the snapshot'), and its own copy is about returning the same tree rather than branching out of the product. Neither route left the Studio.

The queue half is fixed this round and I confirmed it: handedOverExtensions() filters the enumeration, so demo and nodehealth, both with dirty working trees, are not in anybody's queue, and the empty state says why in the rule's own terms ('2 extensions in this Rancher have work in the author's own tree, which is not a review request: a change arrives here when it is pushed for review as a packet'). Only base, which has a packet, is listed. What is not there is the accumulation.
verdicts.defect: Nothing accumulates in the background while the author works. The one material the packet is supposed to have gathered across earlier cycles is the per-hunk prompt provenance, and the packet on base carries none (screen 12 reports 'No prompt recorded for any of this change's 39 lines'). The assembly at the push cannot be exercised either, for the reason in 00-cross-screen-pr-is-the-record. Also worth fixing in the fixture: barn-review-base names packet 1 at refs/barn/packets/1 but the pod has no such ref, so distributionGate() reads the extension as never handed over while the queue and screen 12 show packet 1. I added the ref temporarily to test the gate and removed it again.

verdicts.evidence: Now works. Put a file in the pod whose added line mentions words the brief ruled out ('// w5rc scope probe: alerting and history beyond the brief'). Screen 13's Scope section flagged it: 'This change adds lines that mention what the brief said it was deliberately not doing', listing alerting, history and beyond against verify-w5-scope.ts, each with both resolutions as real buttons: 'That is fine - add it to the brief' and 'Remove it'. It also explains what each does ('Accepting rewrites BRIEF.md: the sentence that ruled this out moves into What changes for them, stamped with today's date' / 'Removing it does not touch the brief - it puts the behaviour to the assistant in this extension's pod and asks for it back out') and states its own limit rather than implying it read the change. Removed the file afterwards.

Per-reviewer state persists and both screens use it. Opening screen 12 recorded a look under my principal in barn-review-base ('looks': {pa5g3hz: {principal: local://user-btc48, sha: 24b3922, at: ...}}), which survived reloads and navigations. The queue row then carried the re-review banner with the count sentence, and its 'Show only what changed since then' link opened screen 12 at ?scope=since&from=<sha> with the chip already active and the diff narrowed from 2 files to 1.

Recorded both sign-offs against packet 1 with the same principal and the gate refused: 'Both sign-offs on packet 1 carry the same person, Default Admin. The two questions are "is it safe?" and "does it work?", and they are two sign-offs precisely because one person answering both is one opinion recorded twice.', with the destination chipped 'Needs a second signer'. With two different principals the same packet moved into the 'Signed off this week' tab instead. The two records are separate objects with their own verdict, principal, name, time and commit, and signing the code left the outcome gate open on screen 12's decision bar. Restored the record afterwards.
